messages:
Meg (Platform): Quick sync — we have a gap in how hosted/dedicated/private adapters should expose auth and cache eviction. Need a small decision before the rollout tomorrow. TL;DR: two options: 1) control-plane mints short-lived capability tokens + routes them to runtimes; 2) carve out a minimal sidecar per deployment to own credentials + small shim API. Pros/cons below. Thoughts?

Sanjay: +1 to sidecar for Private. KMS/HSM integrations mean we shouldn't pass raw creds through hosted control plane. sidecar can use local KMS/HSM and return signed leases.

Tess: sidecar is safer for secrets but increases ops surface. For Hosted we likely won't run sidecars, so we need a clear fallback path. How would we unify the API so callers don't care? :thinking:

Leo: If we do sidecar, let's keep interface minimal. Proposal: HTTP endpoints: 
```
GET /auth/token?scope=<scope> -> {token, expires_at}
POST /cache/invalidate -> 204
GET /health -> 200
POST /metrics/ping -> 202
```
That keeps runtime logic in the runtime; sidecar only does keys + eviction.

Meg (Platform): That matches my thinking. For Hosted -> Dedicated fallback: control-plane can mint a short-lived token with a limited capability claim (e.g., can only use model X at seq_len<=Y). Runtimes accept either sidecar-supplied token OR control-plane token. We need to standardize a claim namespace.

Sanjay: Important: sidecar must not reimplement batching/cache decisions. Runtime should remain the authoritative batching/caching layer. Sidecar only gives ability to evict prefixes and produce credentials. Otherwise we'll diverge.

Tess: Edge-case: on-prem Private clusters that are air-gapped. How do they bootstrap sidecar certs? Option A: manual CSR approval. Option B: offline token + rotation script. I'm leaning manual CSR for first rollout.

Leo: Agree manual CSR to start, but record an offline flow in INF-1234. Also add a small protobuf for the /auth response we can reuse across languages: 
```
message AuthLease {
  string token = 1;
  int64 expires_at = 2;
  repeated string capabilities = 3;
}
```
Keep it tiny so we can implement in Rust/Golang/Python easily.

Meg (Platform): Ops constraints: we need observability hooks. Sidecar must emit a token issuance metric and a cache-invalidate counter. Hosted control-plane path will emit controlplane.issued.token metric. Both should map to the same metric names so billing/usage joins work.

Sanjay: Agreed. Also add a compatibility header so runtime can easily detect origin: `X-Auth-Origin: sidecar|controlplane`. That simplifies logging and fallback logic.

Tess: Can we do a short experiment: implement sidecar stub in dedicated (one team), and a control-plane mint path in hosted. Run both for two weeks and compare ops overhead and latency. If sidecar wins in private & dedicated, we extend.

Meg (Platform): Plan:
- [ ] Tess to spin up lightweight sidecar stub for dedicated env (INF-2340)
- [ ] Leo to draft protobuf + endpoint spec and post RFC (due EOD)
- [ ] Sanjay to write KMS-HSM integration notes for sidecar (due 48h)
- [ ] I will wire up metrics mapping and a compatibility header in the runtime (PR tomorrow)

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-2340 (https://redwood.example/INF-2340) for sidecar stub. Assigned: Tess.

Meg (Platform): If no objections, we go sidecar-minimal + control-plane-fallback pattern. If anyone sees a hard blocker (latency, perf isolation, billing mismatch) shout now. Otherwise I'll call this the decision and update the hosting-adapters doc.

Leo: No blockers from infra side. One note: keep token TTLs short (<= 2m) for high-sensitivity workloads.

Sanjay: +1. We'll test TTL perf impacts.

Tess: OK, proceeding. I'll post a short demo once stub is up. :thumbsup:
